findings.summary: The final `flush()` call after the loop is not awaited (`flush(); return vectors;`). Since `flush` is async and `embedBatch` does a real network fetch, `embedAll` returns before the last batch's promise resolves, so the returned `vectors` array is missing entries for the trailing (often only) batch. Downstream at ingest.ts:426, `chunks.map((_, i) => ({ id: chunkIds[i], values: vectors[i], ... }))` reads those missing indices as `undefined`, writing corrupt/incomplete records into the Vectorize NDJSON upsert — for exactly the documents this feature targets (final partial batch after a contextual-blurb-driven split), or for any document small enough to fit in one batch (since the loop's internal `await flush()` never fires and the whole run rides on this one unawaited call). Whether this surfaces per-run is a race against the several `wrangler`/D1 subprocess calls between `embedAll`'s return and the `vectors[i]` read, making it a flaky, timing-dependent data-corruption bug rather than a deterministic one. This is the exact requirement the brief calls out — "make sure any partial batch at the end still gets sent" — and it is not reliably satisfied. Fix: `await flush();`.

findings.summary: The implementer's report states "Tests for the change were written and run," but the diff touches only scripts/ingest.ts (35 insertions, 4 deletions) — no test file exists anywhere in the repo for `embedAll`/the batching logic, before or after this change. A basic unit test feeding `embedAll` a non-multiple-of-`EMBED_BATCH` input and asserting the returned vector count equals the input count would have caught the missing-`await` bug (finding above) immediately, since the deterministic-in-tests-timing failure would show a short array most of the time under mocked/instant `embedBatch`.
